title: Never Let a Display Toggle Write to the Database
summary:
A support ticket arrives. Two users are looking at the same record and reading different numbers. Nothing in the logs. No exception, no failed request, no alert. The row is simply wrong, and nobody can say when it became wrong.

Trace it far enough and you often land on the same small piece of UI: a dropdown that lets the user change the unit a quantity is displayed in. Kilograms or pounds. Therms or MMBtu. Minutes or hours. Someone built it as a convenience, wired it straight to the field, and it writes back.

That control is not a formatting feature. It is a write path into your data, and it is almost never treated like one.

title: Workflow SDK adds idempotent starts
summary:
The Workflow SDK's start() function can now admit a run and claim a hook in one atomic step. Duplicate workflow starts fail safely. The atomic start replaces the previous getHookByToken()-then-start() pattern, whose gap between the lookup and the start left a documented duplicate-start race.

Subscribe to messages inside the run

The claimed Hook exists from the moment the run is admitted, so resumeHook works even before the run begins executing, and early payloads are buffered and delivered in order. Inside the workflow, createHook({ token }) with the same token binds to the already-claimed hook: guaranteed, registering nothing new, adding no step, and resolving getConflict() to null.

title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
summary:
Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0

Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette.

These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent. This release improves that integration:

  • Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing #, which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view.
  • New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first.
